Supply transfer

Whose inventory is changing hands?

11 chapters with worked investigations

01Price moves at the margin02Liquidity & price impact03Buy/sell pressure04Supply transfer05Early wallet flow06Demand acceleration07Attention conversion08Push, Hold or Fail09Meta saturation10Three basic checks11How to trade the demand wave

01Definition

Supply transfer moves inventory from early holders to later buyers.

02Why it matters

Remaining low-cost inventory can become future sell pressure.

03What to check

  • Early-wallet balances before and after sales
  • Transfers versus executed sells
  • Remaining inventory relative to liquidity

04Healthy / Dangerous

Healthy

Actual sales and new ownership can be traced.

Dangerous

Transfers to related wallets disguise continuing control.

05Beginner mistake

Assuming lower concentration proves independent ownership.

06Takeaway

Track what remains, not just what moved.

ILLUSTRATIVE · NOT A LIVE TOKEN

See the idea

  1. 01

    An early wallet holds 8% of supply.

  2. 02

  3. 03

WORKED INVESTIGATION · ILLUSTRATIVE

Work through the evidence

Mechanism and worked case

A supported early-wallet group holds 20m units, buys 2m, sells 5m, and moves 4m internally. Closing group inventory is 17m. Counting the internal transfer as a sale would incorrectly report 13m.

How to investigate it

Reconcile opening inventory + purchases − sales + outside receipts − outside transfers with closing balances. Mark unexplained differences and add known receiving wallets only when evidence supports linkage. Connect genuine inventory changes with trades and contemporaneous liquidity, not just holder counts.

Check your reasoning — answered

The group sells 5m and independent buyers absorb it while depth stays usable. Has distribution guaranteed a collapse? No. The relevant follow-up is whether demand persists and how much inventory remains.

Trace it externally

Use an explorer and wallet history to trace transfers, trades, and related balances. Meme Fast does not establish common ownership.

Go deeper

Sellable supply is a hypothesis about inventory that may be offered, not an observable list of everyone willing to sell. Holder turnover needs transaction history; a snapshot alone cannot establish it.
